zoe: Quick save — running into inconsistent error surfaces in python SDK 0.9.1 (async). When the service returns a validation error (400) the SDK raises ValidationError but the original HTTP body (json error details) seems lost and retries for 429/5xx aren't happening because the wrapper converts before the transport retry layer sees it. Anyone seen this?

zoe: repro (async):
```py
async with RedwoodClient(token=...) as c:
    try:
        await c.generate.create(prompt=bad_prompt)
    except ValidationError as e:
        # e doesn't have .response.json() or .__cause__ with the httpx Response
        print(type(e), e)
        # nothing useful to surface back to user to explain which field failed
```

zoe: error payload from server (what I expected to see):
```json
{"error": "validation_failed", "details": {"inputs": "too long", "field": "prompt"}}
```

tomas: @zoe thanks for the repro. Two things to check: (1) are you on the sync or async client? async uses httpx and our wrapper historically normalized exceptions which can swallow the original Request/Response. (2) can you paste a short stack trace?

kevin: we noticed similar last week — sync client (requests) surfaces exc.response so you can call .json(), but async -> httpx.Response lives on the original HTTPError which our wrapper used to chain but a recent refactor sets a new exception instance and loses __cause__/__context__.

tomas: short-term fix: set the original exception as __cause__ on the wrapped exception and expose .raw_response attr on RedwoodHTTPError. Example patch I prototyped:
```py
# in transport/error.py
wrapped = RedwoodHTTPError(msg)
wrapped.__cause__ = original_httpx_exc
wrapped.raw_response = getattr(original_httpx_exc, 'response', None)
raise wrapped
```
This preserves chaining and the response for callers.

zoe: I can confirm chained exception would let us do `e.__cause__.response.json()` and extract details. Also, regarding retries: in my case a 429 turned into a ClientRateLimitError which was raised before the retry layer — I think error mapping happens too early. The retry policy should run on transport-level 429/5xx not on post-processed exceptions.

kevin: agreed. Our intended flow: transport -> retry -> response mapping/validation. A bug in 0.9.1 inverted mapping/validation for async clients. I've opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/789 (labels: bug, async, errors)

tomas: thanks @kevin — I'll open a PR to (a) attach __cause__ and raw_response, and (b) move mapping to after retry success. Small snippet for the retry ordering change:
```py
# former: transport.send -> map_response -> retry_if_necessary
# new: transport.send -> retry_if_necessary(map_response)
```
I'll include a feature flag so behavior is opt-in in 0.9.x and default in 0.10.

kevin: PR #790 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/790 — includes tests that assert e.raw_response is not None for async, and that 429 triggers retry before mapping. CI should catch regressions.

sre-bot: CI passed for PR #790 (linux/py38, linux/py310) :white_check_mark: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/790/summary

zoe: awesome — will try the PR build. Thanks for the quick turnaround :pray:. If this lands I can remove my local workaround where I manually inspected httpx internals.

kevin: quick note — consider adding a convenience helper on the error dataclass: `e.as_dict()` that tries raw_response.json() then falls back to parsed fields. That'll help users avoid diving into __cause__.

tomas: good call — I'll add that to the PR.

zoe: tested PR artifact — confirms e.raw_response.json() available and 429 retries now happening. Marking as resolved on my end. Thanks team! :tada:
